meta.title: One Note Between Neighbours
meta.summary: Name any two neighbours on the brightness ladder and you can name the single note that separates them — but only because they're neighbours; skip a rung and the rule breaks.

spans.text: The brightness ladder has a payoff worth spelling out: name any two neighbours on it and you can already name the single note that separates them, without reciting all seven scales from scratch. Six adjacent pairs, six single notes — that's the whole comparison.

Don't let that generalise into "every mode is one note from something I already play".
Nothing New to Learn on the Neck
already showed that's false for Locrian, which needs two changed degrees from natural minor, not one. This rule is about neighbours on the ladder, not about distance from the two scales you own.

Mixolydian to Dorian is the one to keep hold of. It doesn't just change a colour — it changes which chord you're standing on, and that is where the seven split into two.
